text: Chase Alert: A sign-in from a new device in Lagos was blocked. If this wasn't you, verify your identity within 30 min to avoid account suspension: https://chase-secure-verify.top/login

text:
Caller: Hi, this is Daniel from the Wells Fargo fraud department. We've flagged a $1,240 charge at an electronics store in Phoenix. Did you make that purchase?
Victim: No, I didn't.
Caller: Okay, I'm going to stop it for you right now. To confirm you're the account holder, we just sent a six-digit code to your phone. Can you read that back to me?
Victim: It says don't share it with anyone...
Caller: That's right, that message is for outside parties. I'm internal, I'm the one blocking the charge. Go ahead and read it so I can close the case.
label: scam
note: Fake fraud-department call pressuring OTP read-back.

text:
Caller: Ma'am, I'm Officer Grant with the bank's security investigations unit. Your account has been compromised by someone inside your branch, so please don't speak to anyone there.
Victim: Oh my god. What do I do?
Caller: We've opened a protected account in your name. You need to move your savings into it today using a wire, and I'll give you the new account number. Once the investigation is finished in about 72 hours we move it back. Don't tell the teller why you're sending it, just say it's for a family purchase.
Victim: How much?
Caller: The full balance, ma'am. Anything left in the old account is at risk.
label: scam
note: Classic 'safe account' transfer with coaching to lie to the teller.

text:
[Automated voice] This is an urgent message from the Social Security Administration. Your Social Security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity linked to drug trafficking in Texas. A warrant will be issued for your arrest unless you press 1 now to speak to an officer.
[Victim presses 1]
Agent: Badge number 4471, SSA Office of the Inspector General. To keep your benefits active we need to verify your number and move your funds into a federal holding account. This must be done before 5 PM today or local police will be dispatched.
label: scam
note: SSA impersonation with suspension and arrest threats.

text: On Oct 28 my phone suddenly showed 'No Service' around 9 PM. The next morning I went to my carrier store and they said a SIM change had been done on my number the night before, which I never requested. By then someone had reset my online banking password using text codes and sent two transfers of $2,400 and $1,950 from my checking account to someone I don't know. I did not authorize these transfers and did not give anyone my codes. I want the money returned and the transfers investigated.
label: fraud
note: SIM swap leading to unauthorized transfers the consumer did not initiate.

text: I logged into my payment app and found that my email and phone number on the account had been changed and $780 had been sent to an unfamiliar user over three payments on November 4. I was asleep at the time and did not make or approve these payments, and I have never shared my login. The company closed my claim saying the payments were 'authorized' because they came from my account. I am disputing this because someone else took over my account.
label: fraud
note: Unauthorized payments after account credentials were changed by a third party.
